title: Power Struggle After Lenin
welcome_lead: After Lenin's death in January 1924, study how Stalin out-manoeuvred Trotsky and his rivals to dominate the USSR.

walkthroughs.body_html: Lenin's strokes from 1922 and his death on 21 January 1924 left no clear successor. The Testament urged that Stalin be removed as General Secretary, but the Politburo suppressed it. Trotsky's brilliance attracted both admiration and resentment, while Stalin's command of the party machine often went under-estimated.

Stalin allied with Zinoviev and Kamenev against Trotsky (1923-25), then with Bukharin against the United Opposition (1925-27), exiling Trotsky in 1929. The doctrinal contrast — Socialism in One Country vs Permanent Revolution — gave ideological cover to factional manoeuvres.

From 1928 Stalin turned on Bukharin and the Right Opposition, abandoning NEP in favour of forced industrialisation and collectivisation. By 1929-30 Stalin was the dominant figure in Soviet politics, marking the centenary of his birth amid mass adulation while consolidating policies that would transform — and traumatise — Soviet society.

mcqs.q: What did the 1928 Equal Franchise Act do?
options: It gave women the vote on the same terms as men — all adults over 21 — completing the process begun in 1918, which had only enfranchised women over 30 with property.
The 1918 Representation of the People Act gave all women the vote.
The 1928 Act gave women in Britain the vote for the first time.
The NEP was introduced by Stalin to fund the Five-Year Plans.

mcqs.q: Why did Lenin introduce the NEP in 1921?
options: The NEP was Lenin's plan to permanently switch Russia to capitalism.
The NEP was introduced by Stalin to fund the Five-Year Plans.

War Communism had collapsed the economy and provoked the Kronstadt revolt; the NEP allowed limited private trade to restore production and stabilise Bolshevik rule.
